record: POST-HOC DEVELOPMENT OBSERVATION from the closed Val-v1.1 bake-off
why_exploratory: The LIBRARY_DEFAULTS profile was declared DIAGNOSTIC ONLY before any result existed. Its numbers are real measurements on verified GT, but the question they answer was not the question the experiment predeclared, and the hypothesis below was formed after seeing them. Evidence generated this way can motivate a new experiment; it cannot settle the one already closed.

observation.profile: LIBRARY_DEFAULTS -- exact trackers==2.6.0 defaults, no parameter changed
observation.note: The legacy baseline is identical in both rows because it is not re-parameterised by profile; it has one set of production semantics.

hypothesis.statement: EYECU_SCORE_POLICY_V1 may be a poor confidence-policy match for the modern tracker implementations, rather than the modern tracker families being intrinsically worse.
hypothesis.status: HYPOTHESIS ONLY -- untested, generated post hoc
hypothesis.supporting_observation: Under the primary profile the modern trackers receive detections above 0.10 with activation at 0.25 and produce far more track ids (ByteTrackTracker 91/81/97 against 29/23/37 at library defaults). Their detection accuracy also falls (CBIoU DetA 55.00 against 57.89). Both are consistent with a confidence interface that floods them with weak detections, and both are equally consistent with other explanations that have not been tested.
hypothesis.what_would_test_it: Tracking Experiment T2, specified separately and not yet executed.
hypothesis.what_must_not_happen: This hypothesis must not be used to reinterpret the closed experiment, to soften spec 1.1, or to describe LIBRARY_DEFAULTS as having won.

standing_constraints: The closed bake-off keeps its result: KEEP_LEGACY_SUPERVISION_BYTETRACK.
No production change follows from this observation.
No threshold may be tuned on the strength of it.
Any follow-up must be predeclared in its own experiment and labelled post-hoc/development.
